summary: Frontend-only regression test of the MeetingReport.js / TranscriptTab.js component-splitting refactor (manager@supervision.com, cookie-injected session from get_tokens.py). Exercised: all 6 report tabs, Re-scan dialog (open/textarea/cancel/real guided re-scan run to completion), Mark Reviewed, SignOffConfirmModal (blocked + allowed paths), real Sign Off, MoreActionsMenu (include-transcript, Export PDF, Export Transcript, Share), Transcript Full-Text/Speaker toggle, Find & Replace (highlight counter, Next/Prev, no-match disabled state, Replace one + Replace All via API), SpeakerManagerPanel rename/save/discard/reset, per-turn pill reassignment, flip-from-here, swap-all, inline turn text edit + cancel, unsaved-changes guards, Compliance accept/reject/flag + bulk accept, Show-in-transcript cross-tab highlight, summary edit, add/complete/remove action, add comment, and read-only behaviour on a signed-off meeting. NO behavioural regressions found from the refactor - every interaction and data-testid behaved as described. All test data mutations were reverted.

integration_issues.issue: Optimistic update sets the status pill to 'Reviewed' immediately, but the POST + refetch takes 3-5s and the server keeps status 'in_review' until ALL attendees have reviewed, so the pill flips back to 'In Review' and the 'You reviewed this' badge only appears ~5s later. Misleading intermediate state (pre-existing logic moved verbatim into useMeetingReport - not a refactor regression).

issues: All speaker colour swatches in SpeakerManagerPanel render the same grey (#6B7280 default) so the colour legend adds no visual distinction between speakers

design_issues.screen: Meeting Report - signed-off meeting, Transcript tab
issues: When the report is locked (signed off) the whole transcript toolbar is removed: no Find & Replace button, no speaker pills, no SpeakerManagerPanel. Read-only is correct, but losing read-only Find & Replace/search on a locked report is a usability regression risk - confirm this matches pre-refactor intent.

action_items: No functional fixes required for the refactor - regression suite passed.
Optional: avoid the optimistic 'Reviewed' pill flip on Mark Reviewed (only set status locally when allReviewed will become true), and/or show an inline pending state until the refetch resolves.
Optional: give each speaker a distinct colour in SpeakerManagerPanel (all swatches currently grey).
Optional: consider splitting TranscriptTab.js further - still 879 lines (> the 700-line guideline) after the refactor.
critical_code_review_comments: TranscriptTab.js is still 879 lines; the anonymise/split-turn/selection-popup logic is the next natural extraction candidate.
useMeetingReport.js exposes allReviewed (line 81/509) but MeetingReport.js never consumes it (SignOffConfirmModal recomputes unreviewed attendees itself) - dead value, remove or use it in one place.

Client-side speaker-map Save persists the locally cached turns, so a Save performed after a Find & Replace done in another view can re-introduce the pre-replace wording into transcripts.speaker_text (observed once during testing). Pre-existing race; consider re-reading server speaker_text before serializing on save. Verified separately that POST /api/review/{id}/find-replace itself keeps text and speaker_text in sync (both updated, 200 OK).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows passed (0 functional regressions, 0 page/JS errors)

seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Used existing meetings 2f1cc088-0687-48b9-9f40-1dabb5285640 (Demo Manager & Sarah Thompson) and c20802af-17e3-4210-b497-13d09c9e67ec. All mutations reverted: transcript text/speaker_text restored (Tracy x3), speaker labels restored to 'Sarah Thompson', QA_TEST_COMMENT deleted from reviewer_comments, QA_TEST_ACTION removed via UI, summary reverted, both meetings reset to status in_review with attendee reviewed=false via tests/set_review_state.py. NOTE: c20802af was genuinely signed off during the sign-off test (audio deletion pipeline may have run) and 2f1cc088's evidence statuses were reset to 'pending' by the guided re-scan test (87 CQC + 35 CareCert + 6 custom mappings, no duplicates).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie injection works well: run backend/tests/get_tokens.py, save JSON, then page.context.add_cookies for domain evidence-link-4.preview.emergentagent.com. Useful gotchas discovered: (1) SpeakerManagerPanel rename fields are <input> values - assert with input_value()/evaluate_all, NOT inner_text(); (2) speaker-map Save takes ~4s and Mark Reviewed ~3-5s, so wait/poll at least 8-10s before asserting; (3) SpeakerTurnRow pencil/save/cancel buttons only respond to mousedown (use dispatch_event('mousedown')); (4) creating files under /app/backend triggers a uvicorn WatchFiles reload and can time out in-flight API requests - put ad-hoc scripts in /app/tests; (5) one benign 401 on GET /api/auth/me appears on every page load and is auto-recovered by the axios refresh interceptor (likely an artifact of injected cookies) - no user-visible impact; (6) helper scripts: tests/set_review_state.py <meeting_id> <status> email:bool ... to drive review lifecycle.
rca_of_the_issue: No refactor-induced defect found. The two initially suspicious observations were both explained: (a) 'Mark Reviewed did not update the badge' was purely POST+refetch latency (badge appears at ~5.1s, correct after reload); (b) a stray 'Tracey' left in transcripts.speaker_text came from the speaker-map Save persisting stale client-side turns after a full-text Replace, not from the find-replace endpoint (API-level check showed text and speaker_text both updated consistently).
